Rounded to the nearest tenth, what is the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD?$
feedback.worked_solution:
The area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is the sum of the areas of the triangles $△ABD$ and $△BDC$ (see the illustration below).

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13946476/assets/68f5708d49577befe9bac6a7aaf6a54fcdb30dcd344367d2c69b8924093dbb61.png)

 

First we find the area for $△ABD:$ 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABD} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 12\cdot 14\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{42.1}^{∘} \\  & =84\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{42.1}^{∘} \\  & ≈56.315\,8,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Now we find the area for $△BCD:$ 
 

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{BDC} & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 5\cdot 7\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{103.8}^{∘} \\  & =17.5\cdot \operatorname{sin}⁡{103.8}^{∘} \\  & ≈16.994\,8,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to four decimal places.

Finally, we add together the areas of our two triangles to determine the area of $ABCD:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{ABCD} & ={A}_{ABD}+{A}_{BDC} \\  & =56.315\,8+16.994\,8 \\  & =73.310\,6\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, to the nearest tenth, the area of the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is $73.3.$
